reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Wednesday in early September. Nothing special about it. The summer is quietly closing up shop, the light is starting to angle differently in the late afternoon, and most of the people you know are just getting through the week. This is the day. Not the anniversary, not the milestone, not the dramatic before-and-after photo. Just Wednesday.

When I was drinking, I couldn't stand Wednesdays. They were the days that had to be survived, killed, drunk through. There was nothing to do with an ordinary evening except escape it. What sobriety gave me — and this took years to actually feel, not just intellectually understand — is the capacity to be inside a Wednesday without needing to leave it. To cook something. To go for a run. To text a friend back. To sit on the porch and not be doing anything impressive at all.

Durant's line about habit is doing a lot of work here. The life you want isn't waiting on the other side of some big decision. It's being built right now, in the small unglamorous choices of a Wednesday in September. What you do today when nobody is watching, when nothing is on the line, when there's no reason to show up except that you said you would — that's the life. That's actually it.
reflection.meditation: Sit with the ordinariness of today. Notice one small thing you get to do sober that would have been impossible or forgotten a few years ago. Let that be enough.

affirmations: I am building my life in the small choices I make today, not the big ones I imagine later.
Today I can be inside an ordinary day without needing to escape it.
I am someone who shows up, especially when no one is watching.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a plain Wednesday. Grateful for a body that woke up clear, a mind that isn't scrambling to cover tracks, and the strange luxury of having nothing to hide. There was a version of me who couldn't have imagined this being enough — and today it is more than enough.
gratitude.closing: One more ordinary day. That's the whole gift.
